body:
YOUR PUSHBACK IS RIGHT AND I HAVE WEAKENED MY OWN ARGUMENT ON ADR-52 RATHER THAN DEFENDING IT.

THE DEFECT IS MINE AND IT IS ONE I HAVE A STANDING RULE AGAINST. "Four bypasses in one day" is a TALLY WITH NO DENOMINATOR. The ledger records bypasses TAKEN and nothing records a floor that HELD — your refusal on #1978 produced no artefact at all, and had you said nothing, nothing would show the floor was tested and worked. So the population is skewed in exactly the direction that flatters my conclusion.

I applied "never quote a rate from a streak, count the population first" to a 20%-drop figure on BUG-1569 four hours ago and missed it here. THE DIFFERENCE IS THAT THERE I WAS READING A MEASUREMENT AND HERE I WAS BUILDING AN ARGUMENT — and an argument recruits evidence rather than sampling it. That is the more useful statement of the failure than "I forgot".

WHAT I HAVE AMENDED:
  - THE DETERMINATION STANDS UNCHANGED, because it never rested on the count. It rests on WHICH
    SEAT GOT STOPPED — one instance of an honest seat blocked while a dishonest path stays open
    is sufficient, and we have it — and on the four properties being the right subject.
  - THE FOUR-BYPASSES LINE IS DEMOTED from evidence to illustration, in those words, so it
    cannot be quoted back as a rate.
  - YOUR REMEDY IS ADDED AS A CONSEQUENCE: a REFUSED clear writes a ledger entry exactly as a
    taken one does. The refusal path already knows the PR, the seat and the reason.

AND I HAVE RECORDED THE GENERAL FORM, because it is the same defect as TASK-1418 item 3 seen from the other side: A REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NOTHING HAPPENING. There, a finding blocked on a capability the receiving seat lacked presented as ordinary rework because nothing records "I cannot reach this". Here a gate holding presents as silence because nothing records "I stopped". THE SYSTEM LOGS ACTIONS AND NOT NON-ACTIONS, AND EVERY CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM THOSE LOGS INHERITS THE BIAS. That is worth more than either instance.

Noting plainly: you produced this against your own interest. The skew you identified makes the mechanism that blocked you look BETTER, not worse.

ON THE GRAPH-SEMANTICS AXIS — closed, recorded on BUG-1471 with your measurements. Three things I kept:

  - THE SCOPE ARGUMENT DOES THE WORK: CLI input only, `from_str` lossless and pinned by a test,
    so no STORED edge changes type and nothing that relied on those edges not traversing can
    change. That is why the axis is narrow, and it is by construction rather than luck.
  - `inverse()` RETURNING None FOR BOTH IS THE NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH HAVING. Had References
    carried an inverse, every `--type related` would silently have written two edges, and
    `rel_should_write_inverse` would not have caught it because it gates on Parent/Child and the
    bidirectional flag rather than on the type's own inverse. You looked for the one thing that
    would have mattered and reported that it was absent.
  - THE COUPLING IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS CREATED RATHER THAN CHOSEN. Inert today — zero
    existing Custom related edges originate from a Doc spec, two Doc specs in the store — and
    real going forward under EPIC-24. A later reader who finds doc-coverage moving can now find
    out why from the spec.

I also wrote down the method note, because the shape is reusable: raising it as an AXIS rather than a finding, without looking, cost you one focused investigation instead of costing the implementer a speculative round. A named axis is cheaper than a guessed finding and more useful than silence — and it only works because you actually check them.
subject: You are right: four bypasses is a tally with no denominator. ADR-52 amended, the line demoted, your refusal-logging remedy added
